items.text: Surjective endomorphisms
$M$ finitely generated over $A$ commutative, $f\colon M\to M$ surjective $\Rightarrow$ $f$ injective. $M$ is a module over $A[t]$, $t$ acting by $f$.
f(m_i)\ \text{generate; }\ m_i=\sum_j a_{ij}\,f(m_j)\ \text{(surjectivity)}
\det\bigl(\delta_{ij}-a_{ij}f\bigr)\ \text{kills every }m_j,\ \text{hence }M;\qquad \det=1+f\cdot(\cdots)
So $1+f\cdot(\cdots)=0$ on $M$: $f$ is a unit (invertible).
Scheme version: $A$ an algebra of finite presentation over $k$, $u\colon A\to A$ surjective $\Rightarrow$ $u$ is an isomorphism.
k\ \text{noetherian}\Rightarrow A\ \text{noetherian};\qquad J_n=\ker u^n,\quad J_1\subset J_2\subset\cdots\ \text{stationary}\Rightarrow u\ \text{injective}
General $k$: $k=\varinjlim k_i$ with $k_i$ of finite type over $\mathbf Z$; $A$ and $u$ come from $k_i$ for $i$ large, surjectivity too; reduce to the noetherian case.
For an epimorphism in place of a surjection the statement is subtler (Jacobson ring $\mathbf Z$, artinian rings).
Axioms for a class $M$ of morphisms
(a) Stable under base change: if $f\colon X\to S$ is in $M$ then $f'\colon X'=X\times_S S'\to S'$ is in $M$.
\begin{CD} X' @>>> X\\ @V{f'}VV @VV{f}V\\ S' @>>> S \end{CD}
(b) Isomorphisms are in $M$; if $f,g\in M$ are composable, $g\circ f\in M$ (stable under composition).
Affine morphisms satisfy (a), (b): inverse image of an affine open by $g$, then by $f$, is affine.
Consequence 1: stable under products
f_1\colon X_1\to Y_1,\ f_2\colon X_2\to Y_2\ \text{over }S,\ \ f_i\in M\ \Longrightarrow\ f_1\times_S f_2\in M
$f_1\times\mathrm{id}_{Y_2}$ is the base change of $f_1$ by $Y_1\times Y_2\to Y_1$.
f_1\times f_2=(f_1\times\mathrm{id}_{Y_2})\circ(\mathrm{id}_{X_1}\times f_2)\colon X_1\times X_2\to X_1\times Y_2\to Y_1\times Y_2
Consequence 2: the diagonal
\begin{CD} X @>{f}>> Y\\ @. @VV{g}V\\ @. Z \end{CD}
If $g\circ f\in M$ and the diagonal $\Delta_g\colon Y\to Y\times_Z Y$ is in $M$, then $f\in M$.
\Gamma_f=(\mathrm{id}_X,f)\colon X\to X\times_Z Y\ \text{(section of }\mathrm{pr}_1),\qquad f=\mathrm{pr}_2\circ\Gamma_f
In any category, a morphism $X\to Y$ is the same as a section of $X\times Y\to X$.
$\mathrm{pr}_2$ is a base change of $g\circ f\in M$; remains: $\Gamma_f\in M$.
\begin{CD} X @>{\Gamma_f}>> X\times_Z Y\\ @V{f}VV @VV{f\times\mathrm{id}}V\\ Y @>{\Delta_g}>> Y\times_Z Y \end{CD}
The square is cartesian: $(x,y)$ lies in the graph iff $(f(x),y)\in\Delta$, i.e. $f(x)=y$. So $\Gamma_f\in M$ by base change.
Four equivalent conditions on $g\colon Y\to S$
(a) $\Delta_g\in M$; (b) for every $f\colon X\to Y$ in $\mathrm{Sch}/S$, the graph $\Gamma_f\colon X\to X\times_S Y$ is in $M$;
(c) for all $u,v\colon X\rightrightarrows Y$ over $S$, the kernel $K=\ker(u,v)\to X$ is in $M$; (d) after any base change $S'\to S$, every section $\sigma$ of $Y'\to S'$ is in $M$.
\begin{CD} K @>>> Y\\ @VVV @VV{\Delta}V\\ X @>{(u,v)}>> Y\times_S Y \end{CD}
\Delta_g=\ker(\mathrm{pr}_1,\mathrm{pr}_2\colon Y\times_S Y\rightrightarrows Y)
If all diagonals are in $M$: $g\circ f\in M\Rightarrow f\in M$.
Affine morphisms satisfy (a), (b) but diagonals need not be affine: the plane with a doubled origin (two planes glued along the complement of the origin; not separated).
Monomorphisms, surjective morphisms
Monomorphisms: stable under base change and composition; diagonals are monomorphisms; $g\circ f$ mono $\Rightarrow$ $f$ mono.
Surjective (set-theoretically): stable under composition and base change, since $X'\to X\times_S S'$ is surjective on the underlying sets.
Epimorphisms are not stable under base change (injective ring maps do not stay injective under tensor product).
A\ \text{artinian local},\ \mathfrak m\hookrightarrow A,\quad \mathfrak m\otimes_A k=\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2\longrightarrow A\otimes_A k=k\ \text{is zero}
Quasi-compact morphisms
$f$ quasi-compact: the inverse image of every quasi-compact open of $S$ is quasi-compact.
Local on the base: $S=\bigcup S_i$ with $S_i$ quasi-compact open; $f$ quasi-compact $\iff$ all $f^{-1}(S_i)$ are quasi-compact; enough for affine opens $S$.
